name: Digital Asset Manager
author: 2ByteCode

sections.description:
The Digital Asset Manager plugin for WordPress allows you to store, manage, and share all of your digital assets efficiently. This includes themes, plugins, and other files purchased from various marketplaces, with added support for custom taxonomies and templates for enhanced functionality.

Live Demo

  1. Single Page Template
  2. Archive Page Template

Features:

  1. Store and manage all of your digital assets in one place
  2. View detailed information about each asset, such as name, version, date purchased, and source
  3. Easily update your assets to the latest versions
  4. Share assets on social media or via email
  5. Archive and restore assets
  6. Predefined templates for single and archive pages with user override support
  7. Advanced search functionality, including filters for custom taxonomies
  8. Pagination and dropdown category filters for better navigation

Benefits:

  1. Save time and hassle by managing all your digital assets in one place
  2. Keep your assets organized, up-to-date, and easily accessible
  3. Share assets effortlessly with clients or team members
  4. Protect your investment in digital assets by keeping track of them
  5. Centralize your client and asset information for better productivity

Use Cases

  1. WordPress agencies can use the plugin to store and manage the themes and plugins purchased for their clients.
  2. Freelancers can use it to store and organize the digital assets for their projects.
  3. In-house teams can manage company-wide digital resources.

Usage

Once the plugin is activated, you can access it from the Assets menu in WordPress.

  1. Add new assets using the Add Asset menu, where you can upload files and enter detailed information.
  2. View or edit assets by clicking on their titles.
  3. Use predefined single and archive templates for custom display of your assets.
  4. Override templates in your child theme for further customization.

Archive and Single Page Templates

The plugin includes archive and single page templates for the dam-asset post type and associated custom taxonomies (asset-type and asset-tag). These templates can be overridden in your child theme.

Default templates included:
1. single-dam-asset.php
2. archive-dam-asset.php
3. taxonomy-asset-type.php
4. taxonomy-asset-tag.php

Refer to the plugin’s template header comments for override instructions.

Conclusion

The Digital Asset Manager plugin is a versatile tool for WordPress users looking to organize and manage their digital assets. With robust features, user-friendly templates, and seamless integration, it’s ideal for agencies, freelancers, and in-house teams.

Additional Tips

  1. Customize asset library templates by overriding them in your child theme.
  2. Use the included search functionality to quickly find and filter assets.
  3. Enhance navigation with built-in pagination and category filters.
  4. Share assets via social media with prebuilt sharing links.
sections.installation:
This section describes how to install the plugin and get it working.

From within WordPress

  1. Visit Plugins > Add New
  2. Search for Digital Asset Manager
  3. Activate Digital Asset Manager for WordPress from your Plugins menu.
  4. Configure plugin settings under Assets -> Settings.
  5. Visit the new Assets menu and click Add New to start adding your digital assets.

Manually

  1. Download the plugin.
  2. Unzip the file.
  3. Upload the digital-asset-manager/ folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory using cPanel or SFTP/FTP.
  4. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  5. Configure plugin settings under Assets -> Settings.
  6. Visit the new Assets menu and click Add New to start adding your digital assets.
sections.faq:
What do the visibility settings do?

Visibility settings allow you to toggle the public or private visibility of asset post types and taxonomies. This is useful for managing internal-only assets.

Can I override the provided templates?

Yes, templates for single and archive pages, as well as taxonomy and search functionality, can be overridden in your child theme.

Does the plugin support custom taxonomies?

Yes, the plugin includes two custom taxonomies (asset-type and asset-tag) for categorizing and tagging your assets.

  • Tested with WordPress latest version.
  • Added social sharing buttons.
  • Improved search functionality with taxonomy filters.
  • Enhanced Bootstrap 5-based responsive layout.
  • Introduced dropdown category filtering using wp_dropdown_categories.
  • Added support for preselected dropdown options.

1.1.0

  • Imporve the admin interface.
  • Included the single and archive templates.
  • Implemented the Asset tags.

1.0.0

  • First release.
